---
title: "Hello Two Picos"
description: "Host two Picos on Manifold, wire one Wrangler Channel, watch one Pico emit an event that the other Pico consumes and reacts to."
---

## Overview

**Hello Two Picos** is the first *multi-Pico* runtime lab of the Open
Engineering Academy. You will deploy a small **Manifold**
RuntimeEnvironment onto a local **minikube** cluster, host **two named
Pico Elements** inside it (a **producer** and a **consumer**), declare
**one Wrangler-style Channel** that wires them together, and observe
the consumer react to one event emitted by the producer.

This lab is deliberately architecture-first: **two Picos, one Channel,
one wiring relationship, one emitted event, one observed reaction.** It
is the smallest honest "system" milestone beyond the single-Pico
[Hello Pico on Manifold lab](../hello-pico-on-manifold/index.qmd) —
where that lab shows a hosted Pico responding to an external event, this
lab shows two hosted Picos interacting through a Wrangler-declared
Channel.

The lab is **reusable across courses**: it lives at the repository root
under `labs/hello-two-picos/` and is referenced from the
[Manifold course](../../courses/manifold/index.html).

::: {.callout-important title="Scope"}
This lab covers **two** Picos hosted on **one** Manifold
RuntimeEnvironment, wired through **one** Wrangler Channel, with
**one** producer→consumer wiring relationship, one emitted event, and
one observed reaction. Broader multi-Pico topologies, fleet
orchestration, Home Assistant, a Python CLI as the main teaching
surface, and non-Kubernetes runtimes are explicitly out of scope. The
Kubernetes substrate is kept fixed at local minikube throughout.
:::

## What you will produce

A single artifact directory named `hello-two-picos` — matching the
`produces` entry in the lab
[`metadata.yaml`](metadata.yaml). The directory contains:

- the exact Kubernetes manifests applied to the cluster
  (`Namespace`, consumer Pico `Pod`, greeting `Service`, topology
  `ConfigMap`, producer Pico `Pod`),
- the Wrangler-style [topology](downloads/topology.yaml) fragment that
  names the single Channel, the two Picos, and the producer→consumer
  wiring, and
- the captured runtime **Observation** — `observation.txt`, the single
  log line printed by the consumer Pico in reaction to the event
  emitted by the producer Pico.

## Downloads and screenshots

Starter files live under `downloads/`: the Kubernetes manifests, the
Wrangler `topology.yaml` fragment, and `verify.sh` — the automatable
verification script the walkthrough runs in the final step. Screenshots
referenced from the walkthrough live under `screenshots/`. Both
directories are kept even when empty so authors have a consistent place
to add assets.

## Constructive realization

This lab is the **Realization** of a small two-Pico interaction
Definition consistent with the Phase 7 vocabulary taught by the
[Manifold course](../../courses/manifold/index.html). The role
mapping is:

- **Definition** (course-adjacent): two Pico Elements run on a
  Manifold RuntimeEnvironment; one Pico publishes an event onto a
  Wrangler-declared Channel that the other Pico is subscribed to; the
  subscribed Pico produces one Observation in response.
- **Realization** (this lab): a Kubernetes-hosted Manifold `Namespace`
  hosts two `Pod`s (`hello-producer-pico` and `hello-consumer-pico`);
  a `Service` provides the `greeting` Channel; a `ConfigMap` carries
  the Wrangler topology (including the explicit producer→consumer
  `wiring` relationship); a `verify.sh` command asserts the
  single-event / single-reaction contract holds.
- **Element**: `hello-two-picos` — the captured manifests, topology,
  and observation.
